sentences.zh: 陳壽

translations.literal: Chen Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou

sentences.zh: 陳壽，字承祚，巴西安漢人也。

translations.literal: Chen Shou, courtesy name Chengzuo, was a man of Anhan in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou, whose courtesy name was Chengzuo, came from Anhan in Baxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，師事同郡譙周，仕蜀為觀閣令史。

translations.literal: In youth loved learning; studied under same commandery's Qiao Zhou; served Shu as Viewing Pavilion clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from boyhood and studied under Qiao Zhou of his commandery. In Shu-Han he served as a clerk in the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 宦人黃皓專弄威權，大臣皆曲意附之，壽獨不為之屈，由是屢被譴黜。

translations.literal: Eunuch Huang Hao monopolized playing with power; great ministers all bent intent to attach to him; Shou alone did not for him bend; whereby repeatedly was reprimanded and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Huang Hao monopolized power, and high officials fawned on him—except Chen Shou, who would not yield. He was repeatedly censured and demoted.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，有疾，使婢丸藥，客往見之，鄉黨以為貶議。

translations.literal: Met father's mourning; had illness; ordered maid to roll pills; guests went and saw him; village and district thought it demeaning criticism.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he fell ill and had a servant girl prepare his medicine. Visitors saw it, and local opinion condemned the breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 及蜀平，坐是沈滯者累年。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, because of this sank stuck many years.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he remained in disgrace for years on that account.

sentences.zh: 司空張華愛其才，以壽雖不遠嫌，原情不至貶廢，舉為孝廉，除佐著作郎，出補陽平令。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua loved his talent; taking Shou although not distant from suspicion, tracing feeling did not reach demotion and dismissal; raised as Filial and Incorrupt; appointed aide drafter; went out to supplement Yangping magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Hua admired his gifts. Though Chen Shou had not kept clear of scandal, Zhang judged his faults insufficient for permanent ruin, nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, appointed him assistant drafter, and later sent him out as magistrate of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 撰《蜀相諸葛亮集》，奏之。

translations.literal: Composed Shu Chancellor Zhuge Liang Collection, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the collected works of Zhuge Liang, the Shu chancellor, and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 除著作郎，領本郡中正。

translations.literal: Appointed drafter; concurrently headed home commandery's state appraiser.
translations.idiomatic: He was named a drafter and concurrently served as state appraiser for his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 撰魏、吳、蜀《三國志》，凡六十五篇。

translations.literal: Composed Wei, Wu, Shu Three Kingdoms Records, in all sixty-five chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Records of the Three Kingdoms for Wei, Wu, and Shu—sixty-five chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其善敘事，有良史之才。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his good narrating affairs, having good historian's talent.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised his narrative skill and called him a historian of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 夏侯湛時著《魏書》，見壽所作，便壞己書而罷。

translations.literal: Xiahou Zhan at the time was composing Wei Book; seeing what Shou had made, then destroyed his own book and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zhan was drafting a Wei history; when he read Chen Shou's work he tore up his own manuscript and quit.

sentences.zh: 張華深善之，謂壽曰：「當以《晉書》相付耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua deeply approved it, said to Shou, "Ought to take Jin Book and entrust to you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua thought it superb and told him, "The Jin history should be placed in your hands."

sentences.zh: 」其為時所重如此。

translations.literal: He by the time was esteemed thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard he commanded.

sentences.zh: 或云丁儀、丁暠有盛名于魏，壽謂其子曰：「可覓千斛米見與，當為尊公作佳傳。

translations.literal: Some say Ding Yi, Ding Gao had great fame in Wei; Shou said to their sons, "Can seek thousand hu rice give me; ought for your venerable father make fine biography."
translations.idiomatic: Some said that when Ding Yi and Ding Gao had been famous in Wei, Chen Shou told their sons, "Bring me a thousand hu of rice and I will write your fathers a fine biography."

sentences.zh: 」丁不與之，竟不為立傳。

translations.literal: Ding did not give him; in the end did not for them establish biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding family refused, and he never gave them biographies.

sentences.zh: 壽父為馬謖參軍，謖為諸葛亮所誅，壽父亦坐被髡，諸葛瞻又輕壽。

translations.literal: Shou's father was Ma Su's army adviser; Su was by Zhuge Liang executed; Shou's father also sat and was shaved; Zhuge Zhan again slighted Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou's father had been an adviser to Ma Su; when Ma Su was executed by Zhuge Liang, his father was shaven as an accomplice. Zhuge Zhan in turn despised Chen Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽為亮立傳，謂亮將略非長，無應敵之才，言瞻惟工書，名過其實。

translations.literal: Shou for Liang established biography, said Liang general strategy not long, lacked meet-enemy's talent; said Zhan only skilled in writing, name exceeded reality.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhuge Liang's biography Chen Shou wrote that Liang was no master of strategy and lacked the gifts of a field commander, and that Zhuge Zhan was skilled only at calligraphy and more praised than deserved.

sentences.zh: 議者以此少之。

translations.literal: Critics by this thought little of him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 張華將舉壽為中書郎，荀勖忌華而疾壽，遂諷吏部遷壽為長廣太守。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua was about to raise Shou as Palace Secretariat gentleman; Xun Xu envied Hua and hated Shou, then hinted Ministry of Personnel to transfer Shou as Changuang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was about to recommend Chen Shou for the Palace Secretariat. Xun Xu, who resented Zhang, attacked Chen Shou as well and had the Ministry of Personnel move him to be Administrator of Changuang.

sentences.zh: 辭母老不就。

translations.literal: Declined mother's old age, did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded his mother's age and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 杜預將之鎮，復薦之於帝，宜補黃散。

translations.literal: Du Yu about to go to garrison, again recommended him to emperor, ought supplement Yellow Gate or Palisade.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yu was leaving for his frontier command, he recommended Chen Shou to the emperor again, arguing that he should fill a post as Yellow Gate or Palisade attendant.

sentences.zh: 由是授御史治書。

translations.literal: Thereby was appointed censor drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore named drafter to the imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because mother's mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 母遺言令葬洛陽，壽遵其志。

translations.literal: Mother's dying words ordered burial in Luoyang; Shou followed her intent.
translations.idiomatic: Her last wish was to be buried in Luoyang, and Chen Shou obeyed.

sentences.zh: 又坐不以母歸葬，竟被貶議。

translations.literal: Again sat because did not return mother for burial in homeland, in the end was demoted and criticized.
translations.idiomatic: He was attacked again for not taking her body home for burial in the ancestral ground and suffered further disgrace.

sentences.zh: 初，譙周嘗謂壽曰：「卿必以才學成名，當被損折，亦非不幸也。

translations.literal: At first, Qiao Zhou once said to Shou, "You lord must by talent learning complete name; ought meet setback and break—also not misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Qiao Zhou had told him, "You will make your name with learning, but you will also meet reversals—and that is not necessarily a bad thing."

sentences.zh: 宜深慎之。

translations.literal: Ought deeply be cautious of it.
translations.idiomatic: Guard yourself with care."

sentences.zh: 」壽至此，再致廢辱，皆如周言。

translations.literal: Shou reaching here, again brought dismissal and shame—all as Zhou had said.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou's second round of ruin matched Qiao Zhou's warning exactly.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，起為太子中庶子，未拜。

translations.literal: After several years, raised as heir apparent central palace attendant; did not yet invest.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Palace Attendant to the heir apparent but never assumed the post.

sentences.zh: ，病卒，時年六十五。

translations.literal: illness died; at the time age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He then died of illness at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 梁州大中正、尚書郎范頵等上表曰：「昔漢武帝詔曰：『司馬相如病甚，可遣悉取其書。

translations.literal: Liang Province grand state appraiser, Masters of Writing gentleman Fan Ji and others submitted memorial saying, "Formerly Han Emperor Wu edict said: 'Sima Xiangru critically ill, can dispatch to take all his writings.'"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ji, the grand state appraiser for Liang province and a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, jointly memorialized: "Emperor Wu of Han once decreed, 'Sima Xiangru is gravely ill; send someone to collect all his writings.'"

sentences.zh: 』使者得其遺書，言封禪事，天子異焉。

translations.literal: Envoy obtained his leftover writings, spoke feng and shan affairs; Son of Heaven marveled.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy brought back his papers on the feng and shan sacrifices, and the emperor was astonished."

sentences.zh: 臣等案：故治書侍御史陳壽作《三國志》，辭多勸誡，明乎得失，有益風化，雖文豔不若相如，而質直過之，願垂採錄。

translations.literal: We ministers examine: former drafter attendant censor Chen Shou composed Three Kingdoms Records, phrasing much admonition and warning, clarifies gain and loss, benefits customs transformation; although literary splendor not like Xiangru, yet plain straightness surpasses him—we wish it be collected and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: We note that the late drafter-censor Chen Shou wrote the Records of the Three Kingdoms, a work rich in moral judgment that clarifies right and wrong and improves public morals. Its prose is less ornate than Sima Xiangru's, but its honest plainness surpasses him. We beg that it be copied into the imperial collection."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔下河南尹、洛陽令，就家寫其書。

translations.literal: Thereupon edict sent Henan Governor, Luoyang magistrate, to his home copy his book.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the governor of Henan and the magistrate of Luoyang to copy the work at Chen Shou's house.

sentences.zh: 壽又撰《古國志》五十篇、《益都耆舊傳》十篇，餘文章傳於世。

translations.literal: Shou also composed Ancient States Records fifty chapters, Yidu Elders' Traditions ten chapters; remaining essays transmitted in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou also wrote fifty chapters of Records of Ancient States and ten chapters of Traditions of the Elders of Yidu; other essays of his circulated as well.

sentences.zh: 王長文

translations.literal: Wang Changwen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Changwen

sentences.zh: 王長文，字德睿，廣漢郪人也。

translations.literal: Wang Changwen, courtesy name Derui, was a man of Qi in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Changwen, courtesy name Derui, was a native of Qi in Guanghan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少以才學知名，而蕩不羈，州府辟命皆不就。

translations.literal: In youth by talent learning was known, yet dissolute unrestrained; province and headquarters summons all did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: Known young for his scholarship, he was also wild and unbent; he turned down every summons from the province or the commandery.

sentences.zh: 州辟別駕，乃微服竊出，舉州莫知所之。

translations.literal: Province summoned aide-de-camp; then in disguise secretly left; whole province none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: When the province called him as aide-de-camp, he slipped away in disguise and vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 後於成都市中蹲踞齧胡餅。

translations.literal: Later in Chengdu market squatted and gnawed foreign cake.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was seen squatting in the Chengdu market eating flatbread.

sentences.zh: 刺史知其不屈，禮遣之。

translations.literal: Inspector knew he would not bend, with courtesy sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector, seeing that he would not be forced, dismissed him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 閉門自守，不交人事。

translations.literal: Closed gate self-guarded, did not mingle in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his gate and kept to himself, avoiding the world.

sentences.zh: 著書四卷，擬《易》，名曰《通玄經》，有《文言》、《卦象》，可用卜筮，時人比之揚雄《太玄》。

translations.literal: Composed book four volumes, modeled on Changes, named Penetrating Mystery Classic, has Literary Words, Hexagram Images, can be used for divination; people of the time compared to Yang Xiong's Grand Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote four volumes modeled on the Book of Changes, titled the Classic of Penetrating Mystery, with sections on the literary commentary and hexagram images usable in divination. Contemporaries likened it to Yang Xiong's Grand Mystery.

sentences.zh: 同郡馬秀曰：「揚雄作《太玄》，惟桓譚以為必傳後世。

translations.literal: Same commandery Ma Xiu said, "Yang Xiong composed Grand Mystery; only Huan Tan thought it must transmit later generations."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu of his commandery said, "When Yang Xiong wrote the Grand Mystery, only Huan Tan believed it would survive the ages."

sentences.zh: 晚遭陸績，玄道遂明。

translations.literal: Late met Lu Ji, Mystery Way then bright.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lu Ji appeared, and the teaching of the Mystery became clear."

sentences.zh: 長文《通玄經》未遭陸績、君山耳。」

translations.literal: Changwen's Penetrating Mystery Classic has not yet met Lu Ji, Junshan ear."
translations.idiomatic: Changwen's Classic of Penetrating Mystery has not yet found its Lu Ji or Huan Junshan."

sentences.zh: 太康中，蜀土荒饉，開倉振貸。

translations.literal: In Taikang, Shu land famine, opened granaries and relieved with loans.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taikang era famine struck Shu; the government opened the granaries for relief loans.

sentences.zh: 長文居貧，貸多，後無以償。

translations.literal: Changwen dwelt poor; borrowed much; afterward had nothing to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Changwen was poor, borrowed heavily, and could not repay.

sentences.zh: 郡縣切責，送長文到州。

translations.literal: Commandery and county urgently blamed, sent Changwen to province.
translations.idiomatic: The county pressed him and escorted him to the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 刺史徐幹舍之，不謝而去。

translations.literal: Inspector Xu Gan released him; did not thank and left.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xu Gan let him go; he left without a word of thanks.

sentences.zh: 後成都王穎引為江源令。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Chengdu Ying drew him as Jiangyuan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Ying of Chengdu appointed him magistrate of Jiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 或問：「前不降志，今何為屈？

translations.literal: Someone asked, "Before you did not lower your will; now why bend?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "You once refused to humble yourself—why yield now?"

sentences.zh: 」長文曰：「祿以養親，非為身也。

translations.literal: Changwen said, "Salary is to nurture kin, not for self."
translations.idiomatic: Changwen replied, "I take office to support my parents, not for my own sake."

sentences.zh: 」梁王肜為丞相，引為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Rong was chancellor, drew him as retainer gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Rong of Liang became chancellor, he named Changwen a retainer gentleman.

sentences.zh: 在洛出行，輒著白旃小鄣以載車，當時異焉。

translations.literal: In Luoyang going out, always wore white banner small screen to load on cart; at the time thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he rode with a small white silk screen fixed to his carriage, which people found odd.

sentences.zh: 後終於洛。

translations.literal: Later ended in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 虞溥

translations.literal: Yu Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu

sentences.zh: 虞溥，字允源，高平昌邑人也。

translations.literal: Yu Pu, courtesy name Yuanyuan, was a man of Changyi in Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu, courtesy name Yuanyuan, came from Changyi in Gaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 父秘，為偏將軍。

translations.literal: Father Mi, was general of the wings.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Mi was a general of the wings.

sentences.zh: 鎮隴西。

translations.literal: Garrisoned Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was stationed in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 溥從父之官，專心墳籍。

translations.literal: Pu followed father to his post, devoted mind to tomb writings.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu accompanied his father to the post and gave himself entirely to books.

sentences.zh: 時疆場閱武，人爭視之，溥未嘗寓目。

translations.literal: At the time borderlands reviewed arms; people competed to view it; Pu never once placed eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When the army drilled on the frontier, crowds rushed to watch; Yu Pu never looked.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，除郎中，補尚書都令史。

translations.literal: Commandery investigated Filial and Incorrupt; appointed gentleman of the interior; supplemented Masters of Writing capital clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt; he became a gentleman of the interior and then a chief clerk in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尚書令衛瓘、尚書褚䂮-{竝}-器重之。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing director Wei Guan, Masters of Writing Chu Lü both esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wei Guan of the Masters of Writing and Minister Chu Lü both thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 溥謂瓘曰：「往者金馬啓符，大晉應天，宜復先王五等之制，以綏久長。

translations.literal: Pu said to Guan, "Formerly metal horse opened tally; great Jin responded to heaven; ought restore former kings' five-ranks system, to pacify long lasting."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu told Wei Guan, "When the golden-horse omen appeared, Great Jin received Heaven's mandate. You should restore the five ranks of the ancient kings to ensure lasting peace."

sentences.zh: 不可承暴秦之法，遂漢魏之失也。

translations.literal: Cannot inherit violent Qin's laws, follow Han and Wei's errors.
translations.idiomatic: Do not perpetuate the harsh laws of the Qin or repeat the mistakes of Han and Wei."

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「歷代歎此，而終未能改。」

translations.literal: Guan said, "Generations sigh at this, yet in the end could not change."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan answered, "Every age has lamented that, yet none has ever changed it."

sentences.zh: 稍遷公車司馬令，除鄱陽內史。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted capital carriage marshal; appointed Poyang internal historian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to be marshal of the petition coaches and was then named internal historian of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 大修庠序，廣詔學徒，移告屬縣曰：「學所以定情理性而積眾善者也。

translations.literal: Greatly repaired schools, broadly summoned students, shifted notice to subordinate counties saying, "Learning is that whereby fix emotion and rationalize nature and accumulate crowd of good."
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the schools, summoned students widely, and sent a circular to his counties: "Study steadies the feelings, orders the nature, and heaps up every virtue."

sentences.zh: 情定于內而行成於外，積善於心而名顯於教，故中人之性隨教而移，積善則習與性成。

translations.literal: Emotion fixes within and conduct completes without; accumulate good in heart and name displays in teaching; therefore middle men's nature follows teaching and shifts; accumulate good then habit with nature completes.
translations.idiomatic: What is settled within becomes conduct without; goodness stored in the heart wins a name through instruction. Ordinary natures shift with teaching; pile up good deeds and habit becomes second nature."

sentences.zh: 唐虞之時，皆比屋而可封，及其廢也，而雲可誅，豈非化以成俗，教移人心者哉！

translations.literal: In Tang and Yu's time, all compared houses and could enfeoff; when it decayed, then clouds could be executed—is it not transformation to complete custom, teaching shifting human hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun every household deserved a noble rank; when virtue failed, common folk were marked for execution. Is that not proof that transformation makes custom and instruction moves the heart?"

sentences.zh: 自漢氏失-{御}-，天下分崩，江表寇隔，久替王教，庠序之訓，廢而莫修。

translations.literal: Since Han clan lost chariot-reins, realm split and collapsed; south of the river bandits blocked; long replaced kingly teaching; schools' instruction, abandoned and none repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han lost the reins, the realm shattered and the south was cut off by war. Royal teaching languished for ages; schools fell into ruin and none repaired them."

sentences.zh: 今四海一統，萬里同軌，熙熙兆庶，-{咸}-休息乎太和之中，宜崇尚道素，廣開學業，以贊協時雍，光揚盛化。

translations.literal: Now four seas one unification, ten thousand li same track; bright bright hundred myriad; all rest in great harmony's midst; ought esteem and promote Way plain, broadly open learning enterprise, to assist harmonize timely peace, brighten and raise splendid transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four seas are one, the cart tracks run unbroken for a thousand li, and the people bask in the Great Harmony. It is time to honor plain virtue, widen the path of learning, help perfect the age's peace, and spread this splendid transformation."

sentences.zh: 」乃具為條制。

translations.literal: Then fully made articles and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up detailed regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是至者七百餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who arrived were over seven hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: More than seven hundred students enrolled.

sentences.zh: 溥乃作誥以獎訓之，曰：

translations.literal: Pu then composed instructions to encourage and instruct them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu issued a proclamation of encouragement, which said:

sentences.zh: 時祭酒求更起屋行禮，溥曰：「君子行禮，無常處也，故孔子射於矍相之圃，而行禮於大樹之下。

translations.literal: At the time libationer sought again build house to perform rites; Pu said, "Gentleman performs rites, has no fixed place; therefore Confucius shot at Juexiang's orchard, and performed rites under great tree."
translations.idiomatic: When the libationer asked to erect another hall for ritual, Yu Pu said, "The gentleman performs ritual wherever he is: Confucius shot at the Juexiang garden and held ceremony beneath a great tree."

sentences.zh: 況今學庭庠序，高堂顯敞乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover now study courtyard schools, high hall bright and spacious!"
translations.idiomatic: How much more our present academy, with its high, open hall!"

sentences.zh: 溥為政嚴而不猛，風化大行，有白烏集於郡庭。

translations.literal: Pu in government was stern yet not fierce; customs transformation greatly went; white crows gathered at commandery court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu governed firmly but not harshly, and moral influence spread; white crows gathered in the commandery courtyard.

sentences.zh: 注《春秋》經、傳，撰《江表傳》及文章詩賦數十篇。

translations.literal: Annotated Spring and Autumn classic and commentary; composed Jiang Biao Zhuan and essays poems rhapsodies several tens of chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Spring and Autumn Annals and its commentaries, wrote the Traditions from South of the Yangzi, and left several dozen prose and verse pieces.

sentences.zh: 卒于洛，時年六十二。

translations.literal: Died in Luoyang; at the time age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Luoyang at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子勃，過江上《江表傳》於元帝，詔藏于秘書。

translations.literal: Son Bo, crossing river presented Jiang Biao Zhuan to Yuan Emperor; edict ordered stored in palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Bo brought the Traditions from South of the Yangzi to Emperor Yuan after crossing the Yangzi; an edict placed it in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪

translations.literal: Sima Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao

sentences.zh: 司馬彪，字紹統，高陽王睦之長子也。

translations.literal: Sima Biao, courtesy name Shaotong, was Prince of Gaoyang Mu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao, courtesy name Shaotong, was the eldest son of Sima Mu, the Prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 出後宣帝弟敏。

translations.literal: Out to succeed Emperor Xuan's younger brother Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted as heir to Sima Min, younger brother of Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 少篤學不倦，然好色薄行，為睦所責，故不得為嗣，雖名出繼，實廢之也。

translations.literal: In youth devoted learning unwearied, yet loved sex and slighted conduct; was by Mu blamed, therefore could not become heir; although nominally went out to succeed, in reality was discarded.
translations.idiomatic: He studied tirelessly in youth but was lewd and dissolute. Mu censured him and barred him from the succession; though nominally adopted out, he was in effect cast aside.

sentences.zh: 彪由此不交人事，而專精學習，故得博覽群籍，終其綴集之務。

translations.literal: Biao thereby did not mingle in human affairs, but devoted to study; therefore obtained broadly reading crowd of texts, finished his compilation task.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Sima Biao shunned public life and devoted himself to scholarship, reading widely and completing his compilations.

sentences.zh: 初拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: At first appointed cavalry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He first received appointment as a cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，為秘書郎，轉丞。

translations.literal: In Taishi, was palace secretary gentleman, transferred to aide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he was a gentleman of the palace library and then its aide.

sentences.zh: 注《莊子》，作《九州春秋》。

translations.literal: Annotated Zhuangzi, composed Nine Provinces Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Zhuangzi and wrote the Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces.

sentences.zh: 以為「先王立史官以書時事，載善惡以為沮勸，撮教世之要也。

translations.literal: Thought, "Former kings established historians to write times' affairs, record good and evil to serve as discourage and encourage—grasp teaching age's essentials."
translations.idiomatic: He held that "the ancient kings founded historiography to record events, inscribing good and evil to encourage and warn—this is the hinge of governing the age."

sentences.zh: 是以《春秋》不修，則仲尼理之；

translations.literal: Therefore Spring and Autumn not trimmed, then Zhongni ordered it;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Spring and Autumn Annals fell into neglect, Confucius set them in order;

sentences.zh: 《關雎》既亂，則師摯修之。

translations.literal: Guanju already disordered, then Master Zhi trimmed it.
translations.idiomatic: when the "Guanju" ode was corrupted, Master Zhi restored it.

sentences.zh: 前哲豈好煩哉？

translations.literal: Former sages how loved trouble!
translations.idiomatic: Did the sages relish such toil?

sentences.zh: 蓋不得已故也。

translations.literal: In the end it was because they could not do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: They had no choice."

sentences.zh: 漢氏中興，訖于建安，忠臣義土亦以昭著，而時無良史，記述煩雜，譙周雖已刪除，然猶未盡，安順以下，亡缺者多。

translations.literal: Han clan restoration, down to Jian'an, loyal ministers and righteous knights also thereby shone bright, yet the time lacked good historians; records were vexed and mixed; Qiao Zhou although already deleted, yet still not exhaustive; from An and Shun down, missing many.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han restoration to the Jian'an era, loyal men made shining names, yet there was no worthy historian; accounts grew tangled. Qiao Zhou pruned them but left the job unfinished, and from the An and Shun reigns onward much was lost."

sentences.zh: 」彪乃討論眾書，綴其所聞，起于世祖，終於孝獻，編年二百，錄世十二，通綜上下，旁貫庶事，為紀、志、傳凡八十篇，號曰《續漢書》。

translations.literal: Biao then discussed crowd of books, stitched what he heard, rising from Shizu, ending at filial Xian, annals two hundred years, recording generations twelve, threading through high and low, sideways penetrating myriad affairs, made annals, treatises, biographies in all eighty chapters, titled Continued Han Book.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao collated the sources and arranged what he had learned from Emperor Guangwu through Emperor Xian—two hundred years in annalistic form, twelve reigns, linking high policy with humble detail in annals, treatises, and biographies: eighty chapters titled the Continued Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，武帝親祠南郊，彪上疏定議，語在《效祀志》。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning, Emperor Wu personally sacrificed south suburb; Biao submitted memorial fixing discussion; words are in Suburban Sacrifice Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi, when Emperor Wu sacrificed at the southern suburb in person, Sima Biao memorialized with a settled opinion—the text appears in the treatise on suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later appointed gentleman cavalier attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed gentleman cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末年卒，時所六十餘。

translations.literal: At Emperor Hui's end years died; at the time place sixty odd.
translations.idiomatic: He died toward the end of Emperor Hui's reign, aged over sixty.

sentences.zh: 初，譙周以司馬遷《史記》書周秦以上，或采俗語百家之言，不專據正經，周於是作《古史考》二十五篇，皆憑舊典，以糾遷之謬誤。

translations.literal: At first, Qiao Zhou because Sima Qian's Records of the Historian wrote Zhou and Qin and above, sometimes gathered vulgar sayings hundred schools' words, not solely relied on correct classics; Zhou thereupon composed Ancient History Examination twenty-five chapters, all relying on old canons, to correct Qian's errors.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou had objected that Sima Qian's Records, in treating antiquity down through Zhou and Qin, sometimes drew on vulgar lore and the hundred schools rather than orthodox classics, so he wrote twenty-five chapters of Ancient History Examined, grounding each point in older texts to correct Sima Qian's mistakes.

sentences.zh: 彪復以周為未盡善也，條《古史考》中凡百二十二事為不當，多據《汲塚紀年》之義，亦行於世。

translations.literal: Biao again took Zhou as not exhaustively good; itemized Ancient History Examination inside in all hundred twenty-two matters as improper, mostly according to Ji Tomb Bamboo Annals' meaning; also circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao still found Qiao Zhou incomplete and listed 122 points in Ancient History Examined as wrong, relying chiefly on the Ji Tomb Bamboo Annals; his critique too circulated.

sentences.zh: 王隱

translations.literal: Wang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin

sentences.zh: 王隱，字處叔，陳郡陳人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yin, courtesy name Shushu, was a man of Chen in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, courtesy name Shushu, was a native of Chen in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 世寒素。

translations.literal: Generations cold and plain.
translations.idiomatic: His family was of humble station.

sentences.zh: 父銓，曆陽令，少好學，有著述之志，每私錄晉事及功臣行狀，未就而卒。

translations.literal: Father Quan, Liyang magistrate; in youth loved learning; had writing's ambition; often privately recorded Jin affairs and merit officials' conduct accounts; not finished then died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Quan, magistrate of Liyang, loved learning and hoped to write a history; he privately noted Jin events and the deeds of eminent men but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 隱以儒素自守，不交勢援，博學多聞，受父遺業，西都舊事多所諳究。

translations.literal: Yin by Confucian plainness self-guarded, did not mingle with power's aid; broad learning much hearing; received father's leftover task; western capital old affairs much familiarly studied.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin lived plainly as a scholar, shunned powerful patrons, read widely, inherited his father's project, and knew the old stories of the western capital in depth.

sentences.zh: 建興中，過江，丞相軍諮祭酒涿郡祖納雅相知重。

translations.literal: In Jianxing, crossed the river; chancellor army advisory libationer Zhuo commandery Zu Na elegantly mutually knew and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing he crossed the Yangzi, and Zu Na of Zhuo commandery, the chancellor's army advisory libationer, became his close friend and patron.

sentences.zh: 納好博弈，每諫止之。

translations.literal: Na loved yi and bo; each time admonished to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na loved board games, and Wang Yin often urged him to give them up.

sentences.zh: 納曰：「聊用忘憂耳。

translations.literal: Na said, "Just use to forget worry."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Na said, "They help me forget my cares—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」隱曰：「蓋古人遭時，則以功達其道；

translations.literal: Yin said, "Covering ancients meeting the age, then by merit extend their Way;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin replied, "The ancients, when the times favored them, realized the Way through achievement;

sentences.zh: 不遇，則以言達其才，故否泰不窮也。

translations.literal: not meeting, then by words extend their talent; therefore misfortune and fortune not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: when they were blocked, they showed their gifts in writing—so they were never left without recourse."

sentences.zh: 當今晉未有書，天下大亂，舊事蕩滅，非凡才所能立。

translations.literal: Now Jin has no book; realm great chaos; old affairs swept away—not extraordinary talent can establish.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is no Jin history; the realm is in chaos and the past is being lost—no ordinary talent could set it down."

sentences.zh: 君少長五都，游宦四方，華夷成敗皆在耳目，何不述而裁之！

translations.literal: You lord young grew in five capitals, wandered office four directions; Hua and Yi success and defeat all in ear and eye—why not narrate and trim them!
translations.idiomatic: You grew up in the great cities and served across the empire; the rise and fall of Chinese and barbarian alike has passed before your eyes—why not commit it to writing?"

sentences.zh: 應仲遠作《風俗通》，崔子真作《政論》，蔡伯喈作《勸學篇》，史遊作《急就章》，猶行於世，便為沒而不朽。

translations.literal: Ying Zhongyuan composed Customs and Usages, Cui Zizhen composed Political Treatise, Cai Bojie composed Exhortation to Study, Shi You composed Rapid Writing Primer—still circulated in the age; then became dead yet not rotten.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao wrote the Comprehensive Meaning of Customs, Cui Shi the Political Treatise, Cai Yong the essay urging study, Shi You the literacy primer—they still circulate and keep their authors alive after death."

sentences.zh: 當其同時，人豈少哉？

translations.literal: At their same time, people how few!
translations.idiomatic: Were talented men rare in their day?

sentences.zh: 而了無聞，皆由無所述作也。

translations.literal: Yet utterly without fame—all because without what they narrated and composed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we hear nothing of them because they left no writings."

sentences.zh: 故君子疾沒世而無聞，《易》稱自強不息，況國史明乎得失之跡，何必博弈而後忘憂哉」納喟然歎曰：「非不悅子道，力不足也。

translations.literal: Therefore gentleman hates dying age without fame; Changes praises self-strengthening without rest; moreover state history clarifies gain and loss's traces—why must yi and bo then forget worry!" Na sighed and sighed saying, "Not that I do not delight in your Way—strength not sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman dreads leaving the world unknown; the Book of Changes praises unstriving effort—how much more a national history that sets gain and loss in clear light! Must you gamble to forget sorrow?" Zu Na sighed, "I do not reject your path—I lack the strength to follow it."

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏薦隱。

translations.literal: Then submitted memorial recommending Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon memorialized to recommend Wang Yin.

sentences.zh: 元帝以草創務殷，未遑史官，遂寢不報。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan because founding tasks abundant, no leisure for historians; then slept without reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was too busy founding the court to appoint historians and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 太興初，典章稍備，乃召隱及郭璞俱為著作郎，令撰晉史。

translations.literal: Taixing beginning, statutes gradually complete; then summoned Yin and Guo Pu both as drafters, ordered compose Jin history.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing, as institutions took shape, the throne summoned Wang Yin and Guo Pu as drafters and ordered them to compile the Jin history.

sentences.zh: 豫平王敦功，賜爵平陵鄉侯。

translations.literal: Participated in pacifying Wang Dun's merit; granted noble rank village marquis of Pingling.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in suppressing Wang Dun he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Pingling.

sentences.zh: 時著作郎虞預私撰《晉書》，而生長東南，不知中朝事，數訪於隱，並借隱所著書竊寫之，所聞漸廣。

translations.literal: At the time drafter Yu Yu privately composed Jin Book, yet grew in southeast, did not know central court affairs; repeatedly consulted Yin, and borrowed Yin's composed books secretly copied them; what he heard gradually broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu, another drafter, was privately writing a Jin history. Raised in the southeast, he knew little of the old central court; he often questioned Wang Yin and copied his manuscripts in secret, widening his knowledge.

sentences.zh: 是後更疾隱，形於言色。

translations.literal: After this further hated Yin, shown in words and face.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he turned against Wang Yin and showed it openly.

sentences.zh: 預既豪族，交結權貴，共為朋黨，以斥隱，竟以謗免，黜歸於家。

translations.literal: Yu already powerful clan, intertwined with power nobles, together made faction, to expel Yin; in the end by slander dismissed, demoted returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu was a magnate with ties to the mighty; he formed a clique to drive Wang Yin out and had him dismissed on a slander charge and sent home.

sentences.zh: 貧無資用，書遂不就，乃依征西將軍庾亮于武昌。

translations.literal: Poor without resources; book then not completed; then relied on General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Destitute, he could not finish the book until he attached himself to Yu Liang, the General Who Conquers the West, at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 亮供其紙筆，書乃得成，詣闕上之。

translations.literal: Liang supplied his paper and brush; book then could be completed; went to palace gate presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang supplied paper and ink; the work was completed and presented at court.

sentences.zh: 隱雖好著述，而文辭鄙拙，蕪舛不倫。

translations.literal: Yin although loved writing, yet phrasing vulgar and clumsy, weedy and wrong not ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin loved to write, but his prose was crude and confused.

sentences.zh: 其書次第可觀者，皆其父所撰；

translations.literal: His book's order what can be viewed—all was his father's composition;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever in the book reads well came from his father's pen;

sentences.zh: 文體混漫義不可解者，隱之作也。

translations.literal: literary style mixed diffuse meaning not understandable—Yin's composition.
translations.idiomatic: the muddled, unintelligible passages are Wang Yin's own.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒於家。

translations.literal: Age over seventy; died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 隱兄瑚，字處仲。

translations.literal: Yin's elder brother Hu, courtesy name Zhongchu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin's elder brother Wang Hu, courtesy name Zhongchu

sentences.zh: 少重武節，成都王穎舉兵向洛，以為冠軍參軍，積功，累遷遊擊將軍，與司隸滿奮、河南尹周馥等俱屯大司馬門，以衛宮掖。

translations.literal: In youth esteemed martial integrity; Prince of Chengdu Ying raised troops toward Luoyang; made him champion army adviser; accumulated merit; promoted repeatedly to mobile-corps general; with Metropolitan Governor Man Fen, Henan Governor Zhou Fu and others together garrisoned Grand Marshal gate, to guard palace side.
translations.idiomatic: He honored military duty from youth. When Prince Ying of Chengdu marched on Luoyang, Wang Hu became an army adviser to the champion general, won promotion to mobile-corps general, and with Metropolitan Governor Man Fen, Henan Governor Zhou Fu, and others held the gate of the Grand Marshal's compound to defend the palace.

sentences.zh: 時上官已縱暴，瑚與奮等共謀除之，反為所害。

translations.literal: At the time Shangguan Ji ran amok; Hu with Fen and others together plotted to remove him; contrary was by him harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangguan Ji ran amok, Wang Hu and Man Fen plotted to kill him but were killed instead.

sentences.zh: 虞預

translations.literal: Yu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu

sentences.zh: 虞預，字叔甯，征士喜之弟也，本名茂，犯明穆皇后母諱，故改焉。

translations.literal: Yu Yu, courtesy name Shuning, was summoned gentleman Xi's younger brother; original name Mao; violated Empress Mingmu's mother's taboo; therefore changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu, courtesy name Shuning, was the younger brother of the recluse Yu Xi. His original name was Mao, but he changed it to avoid the personal name of Empress Mingmu's mother.

sentences.zh: 預十二而孤，少好學，有文章。

translations.literal: Yu at twelve then orphaned; in youth loved learning; had literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at twelve, he loved learning and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 余姚風俗，各有朋黨，宗人共薦預為縣功曹，欲使沙汰穢濁。

translations.literal: Yuyao customs, each had factions; clan men together recommended Yu as county merit clerk, wished to make him sift filth.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyao was ridden with factions; his kinsmen jointly nominated him county merit clerk hoping he would purge corruption.

sentences.zh: 預書與其從叔父曰：「近或聞諸君以預入寺，便應委質，則當親事，不得徒已。

translations.literal: Yu wrote to his junior uncle saying, "Recently perhaps heard gentlemen because Yu entered temple, then ought to pledge substance; then ought personally serve affairs; cannot in vain stop."
translations.idiomatic: Yu wrote his uncle: "I hear you mean to bring me into office; if I accept, I must take real responsibility—I cannot serve in name only."

sentences.zh: 然預下愚，過有所懷。

translations.literal: Yet Yu lowest foolishness, excess has what is in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: I am a dull man, yet I have grave doubts."

sentences.zh: 邪党互瞻，異同蜂至，一旦差跌，眾鼓交鳴。

translations.literal: Evil factions mutually watch; same and different swarm arrive; once stumble, crowd drums cross sound.
translations.idiomatic: Rival cliques watch one another; agreement and strife swarm in; one misstep and every drum will beat against you."

sentences.zh: 毫釐之失，差以千里，此古人之炯戒，而預所大恐也。

translations.literal: Hair and li's loss, errs by thousand li; this ancients' bright warning—yet Yu's great fear.
translations.idiomatic: A hair's-breadth error becomes a thousand-li blunder—the ancients warned us sharply, and that is what I dread."

sentences.zh: 」卒如預言，未半年，遂見斥退。

translations.literal: In the end as Yu foretold; not half a year, then was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded as he predicted: within half a year he was cashiered.

sentences.zh: 太守庾琛命為主簿，預上記陳時政所失，曰：「軍寇以來，賦役繁數，兼值年荒，百姓失業，是輕徭薄斂，寬刑省役之時也。

translations.literal: Administrator Yu Chen ordered him as chief clerk; Yu submitted memorial stating current government's losses, saying, "Since military bandits, levies and corvée numerous; also met year famine; hundred surnames lost occupations—this is light corvée thin exactions, lenient punishments reduce labor time."
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Yu Chen made him chief clerk. Yu submitted a report on policy failures: "Since the wars, taxes and labor service have multiplied while famine has thrown people out of work—this is the moment to ease levies, lighten punishments, and cut corvée."

sentences.zh: 自頃長吏輕多去來，送故迎新，交錯道路。

translations.literal: Since recently senior clerks lightly much come and go; send off old welcome new, cross on roads.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates lately change post at whim; send-offs and welcomes choke the roads."

sentences.zh: 受迎者惟恐船馬之不多，見送者惟恨吏卒之常少。

translations.literal: Those welcomed fear only boats and horses not many; those sent off hate only clerks and soldiers always few.
translations.idiomatic: Incoming officials want ever more boats and horses; outgoing parties complain there are never enough attendants."

sentences.zh: 窮奢竭費謂之忠義，省煩從簡呼為薄俗，轉相放效，流而不反，雖有常防，莫肯遵修。

translations.literal: Exhaust luxury exhaust expense called loyalty and righteousness; save bother follow simplicity called mean custom; turn and imitate each other, flow and not return; although have constant guard, none willing follow and practice.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance is hailed as loyalty, thrift mocked as stinginess; the fashion spreads unchecked and even standing rules go unheeded."

sentences.zh: 加以王途未夷，所在停滯，送者經年，永失播植。

translations.literal: Add king's road not pacified; everywhere stop and stick; senders span years; forever lose sowing and planting.
translations.idiomatic: The royal highways are still unsafe; processions stall for years while farmers abandon their fields."

sentences.zh: 一夫不耕，十夫無食，況轉百數，所妨不訾。

translations.literal: One man not plows, ten men lack food; moreover turn hundred count—what is harmed not countable.
translations.idiomatic: If one man does not till, ten go hungry; when hundreds are tied up in escorts, the waste is beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜勒屬縣，若令、尉先去官者，人船吏侍皆具條列，到當依法減省，使公私允當。

translations.literal: I foolish say ought order subordinate counties: if magistrate or captain first leave office, people boats clerk attendants all fully itemize list; arrival ought according to law reduce and save, make public and private fitting proper.
translations.idiomatic: Order every county: when a magistrate or captain departs, list every man, boat, and attendant required for the escort and cut the totals by law so public need and private burden stay fair."

sentences.zh: 又今統務多端，動加重制，每有特急，輒立督郵。

translations.literal: Moreover now overseeing affairs many ends; move and add heavy regulations; each time specially urgent, then establish supervising post.
translations.idiomatic: Administration grows ever more complex with extra controls; every emergency spawns another supervising courier."

sentences.zh: 計今直兼三十餘人，人船吏侍皆當出官，益不堪命，宜復減損，嚴為之防。

translations.literal: Count now straight concurrent thirty-odd people; people boats clerk attendants all ought leave office; more unbearable commands; ought again reduce and cut, strictly for it guard.
translations.idiomatic: Some thirty-odd posts now overlap; each demands clerks, boats, and runners from the offices—the people cannot bear it. Slash the numbers and enforce strict limits."

sentences.zh: 」琛善之，即皆施行。

translations.literal: Chen approved it; immediately all implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chen approved and put the proposals into effect.

sentences.zh: 太守紀瞻到，預復為主簿，轉功曹史。

translations.literal: Administrator Ji Zhan arrived; Yu again was chief clerk; transferred to merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Zhan became administrator, Yu Yu again served as chief clerk, then as merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，不行。

translations.literal: Investigated Filial and Incorrupt; did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated Filial and Incorrupt but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 安東從事中郎諸葛恢、參軍庾亮等薦預，召為丞相行參軍兼記室。

translations.literal: Eastern Pacification retainer gentleman Zhuge Hui, army adviser Yu Liang and others recommended Yu; summoned as chancellor mobile army adviser concurrent secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui, the retainer gentleman of the Eastern Pacification general, and Yu Liang the army adviser recommended him; he was called to serve as a mobile army adviser to the chancellor and concurrently as secretary.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，服竟，除佐著作郎。

translations.literal: Met mother's mourning; mourning finished; appointed aide drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he became assistant drafter.

sentences.zh: ，大旱，詔求讜言直諫之士，預上書諫曰：

translations.literal: great drought; edict sought blunt words straight remonstrance gentlemen; Yu submitted memorial remonstrating saying:
translations.idiomatic: A great drought struck; the court called for blunt counsel, and Yu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 預以寇賊未平，當須良將，又上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yu because bandits not pacified, ought need good generals; again submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Because rebels were still active and able generals were needed, he also memorialized:

sentences.zh: 轉琅邪國常侍，遷秘書丞、著作郎。

translations.literal: Transferred Langye kingdom regular attendant; promoted palace secretary aide, drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He became a regular attendant in the Langye princedom, then palace secretary aide and drafter.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，夏旱，詔眾官各陳致雨之意。

translations.literal: Xianhe beginning, summer drought; edict crowd officials each state bring rain's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe a summer drought led the throne to ask every official how to bring rain.

sentences.zh: 預議曰：

translations.literal: Yu debated saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu offered his view:

sentences.zh: 從平王含，賜爵西鄉侯。

translations.literal: Followed pacifying Wang Han; granted noble rank marquis of Xixiang.
translations.idiomatic: For helping to crush Wang Han he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xixiang.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作亂，預先假歸家，太守王舒請為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Su Jun made rebellion; Yu beforehand took leave returned home; Administrator Wang Shu requested him as advisory army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rebelled, Yu Yu was on leave at home; Administrator Wang Shu engaged him as advisory army adviser.

sentences.zh: 峻平，進爵平康縣侯，遷散騎侍郎，著作如故。

translations.literal: Jun pacified; advanced noble rank county marquis of Pingkang; promoted gentleman cavalier attendant; drafting as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell he was advanced to county marquis of Pingkang and promoted gentleman cavalier attendant while keeping his drafting duties.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍，仍領著作。

translations.literal: Appointed regular cavalier attendant; still headed drafting.
translations.idiomatic: He was named regular cavalier attendant and continued to supervise the history office.

sentences.zh: 以年老歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Because old age returned; died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with age and died at home.

sentences.zh: 預雅好經史，憎疾玄虛，其論阮籍裸袒，比之伊川被髮，所以胡虜遍於中國，以為過衰周之時。

translations.literal: Yu elegantly loved classics and histories; hated and detested dark emptiness; his discussing Ruan Ji naked torso, compared to Yichuan disheveled hair; whereby Hu captives spread through Middle Kingdom; thought exceeded declining Zhou's time.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu loved the classics and histories and detested empty Daoist talk. He likened Ruan Ji's nakedness to the disheveled hair that foretold barbarian invasion in the Book of Changes, and blamed such conduct for the spread of non-Chinese power across China—worse, he thought, than the late Zhou decay.

sentences.zh: 著《晉書》四十餘卷、《會稽典錄》二十篇、《諸虞傳》十二篇，皆行於世。

translations.literal: Composed Jin Book forty-odd chapters, Kuaiji Standard Records twenty pieces, Various Yu Traditions twelve chapters—all circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than forty chapters of a Jin history, twenty essays of Kuaiji Standard Records, and twelve chapters of Traditions of the Yu Clan—all of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦碑誄論難數十篇。

translations.literal: What he composed poems rhapsodies stele dirges treatises disputation several tens of chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He also left several dozen poems, rhapsodies, inscriptions, dirges, essays, and polemics.

sentences.zh: 孫盛

translations.literal: Sun Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng

sentences.zh: 孫盛，字安國，太原中都人。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng, courtesy name Anguo, was a man of Zhongdu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng, courtesy name Anguo, came from Zhongdu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖楚，馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Chu, Fengyi Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sun Chu was Administrator of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 父恂，潁川太守。

translations.literal: Father Xun, Yingchuan Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Xun was Administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 恂在郡遇賊，被害。

translations.literal: Xun in commandery met bandits; was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xun was killed by bandits while in office.

sentences.zh: 盛年十歲，避難渡江。

translations.literal: Sheng age ten, fled disaster crossed river.
translations.idiomatic: At ten Sun Sheng fled south across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學，善言名理。

translations.literal: When grown, broad learning; good at speaking name principles.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was widely read and skilled in arcane philosophy.

sentences.zh: 于時殷浩擅名一時，與抗論者，惟盛而已。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Hao monopolized fame one generation; with him opposing in debate—only Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao then dominated intellectual fashion; only Sun Sheng could argue him to a standstill.

sentences.zh: 盛嘗詣浩談論，對食，奮擲麈尾，毛悉落飯中，食冷而復暖者數四，至暮忘餐，理竟不定。

translations.literal: Sheng once visited Hao to discuss; facing food; vigorously threw deer-tail; hairs all fell in rice; food cold then again warmed four times; reached evening forgot meal; principle in the end not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Sheng debated Yin Hao over a meal, gesticulating so wildly that the hairs of his fly-whisk fell into the rice. The food cooled and was reheated four times; by nightfall they had forgotten to eat and still reached no conclusion.

sentences.zh: 盛又著醫卜及《易象妙於見形論》，浩等竟無以難之，由是遂知名。

translations.literal: Sheng also composed medicine divination and Treatise on Change Images Subtler than Visible Form; Hao and others in the end had nothing to challenge him; whereby then became known.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote on medicine, divination, and the thesis that the images of the Changes are subtler than outward form—Yin Hao could not refute him, and his reputation was made.

sentences.zh: 起家佐著作郎，以家貧親老，求為小邑，出補瀏陽令。

translations.literal: Rose from family as aide drafter; because family poor kin old, sought to be small town; went out to supplement Liuyang magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He began as assistant drafter but, being poor with aged parents, asked for a minor post and became magistrate of Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 太守陶侃請為參軍。

translations.literal: Administrator Tao Kan requested him as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Tao Kan took him on as army adviser.

sentences.zh: 庾亮代侃，引為征西主簿，轉參軍。

translations.literal: Yu Liang replaced Kan; drew him as General Who Conquers the West chief clerk; transferred to army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Liang succeeded Tao Kan, Sun Sheng became his chief clerk, then army adviser.

sentences.zh: 時丞相王導執政，亮以元舅居外，南蠻校尉陶稱讒構其間，導、亮頗懷疑貳。

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Wang Dao held government; Liang as chief maternal uncle dwelt outside; South Man Colonel Tao Cheng slandered and framed between them; Dao, Liang quite harbored suspicion and two hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Dao held power while Yu Liang, the emperor's uncle by marriage, commanded the frontier. Tao Cheng, the South Man colonel, sowed discord, and Wang Dao and Yu Liang grew mutually suspicious.

sentences.zh: 盛密諫亮曰：「王公神情朗達，常有世外之懷，豈肯為凡人事邪！

translations.literal: Sheng secretly remonstrated Liang saying, "Royal duke spirit bearing clear and open; constantly has beyond-the-world's bosom—how willing to do vulgar men's affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng urged Yu Liang in private: "His Grace Wang Dao is open-minded and lives above petty quarrels—why would he stoop to ordinary intrigue?"

sentences.zh: 此必佞邪之徒欲間內外耳。

translations.literal: This must be flatterer wicked fellows wishing to divide inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely slander meant to split court from camp."

sentences.zh: 」亮納之。

translations.literal: Liang accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang took the advice.

sentences.zh: 庾翼代亮，以盛為安西諮議參軍，尋遷廷尉正。

translations.literal: Yu Yi replaced Liang; took Sheng as General Who Pacifies the West advisory army adviser; soon promoted rectifier of the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yi succeeded Yu Liang, Sun Sheng became advisory army adviser to the General Who Pacifies the West and soon rectifier at the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 會桓溫代翼，留盛為參軍，與俱伐蜀，軍次彭模，溫自以輕兵入蜀，盛領贏老輜重在後，賊數千忽至，眾皆遑遽。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen replaced Yi, kept Sheng as army adviser, with him together attacked Shu; army halted at Pengmo; Wen himself with light troops entered Shu; Sheng led weak old baggage train behind; bandits several thousand suddenly arrived; crowd all flustered.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen kept him as army adviser for the Shu campaign. At Pengmo, Huan Wen took light troops forward while Sun Sheng shepherded the baggage train of veterans. Thousands of enemy suddenly appeared and the column panicked.

sentences.zh: 盛部分諸將，並力距之，應時敗走。

translations.literal: Sheng deployed various generals; joined strength resisted them; in response time defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng rallied the officers, held the line, and the enemy broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，賜爵安懷縣侯，累遷溫從事中郎。

translations.literal: Shu pacified; granted noble rank county marquis of Anhuai; promoted repeatedly to Wen's retainer gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he was enfeoffed as county marquis of Anhuai and rose to retainer gentleman under Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 從入關平洛，以功進封吳昌縣侯，出補長沙太守。

translations.literal: Followed enter passes pacify Luoyang; by merit advanced enfeoffment county marquis of Wuchang; went out to supplement Changsha Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Huan Wen through the passes to secure Luoyang, was advanced to county marquis of Wuchang for merit, and became Administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 以家貧，頗營資貨，部從事至郡察知之，服其高名而不劾之。

translations.literal: Because family poor, quite managed goods and wealth; department attendant arrived commandery investigated and knew; submitted to his high name and did not impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he dabbled in trade for profit. The regional investigator found out but, respecting his reputation, brought no charges.

sentences.zh: 盛與溫箋，而辭旨放蕩，稱州遣從事觀采風聲，進無威鳳來儀之美，退無鷹鸇搏擊之用，徘徊湘川，將為怪鳥。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Wen note, yet wording wanton; said province sent attendant to observe gather wind sounds; advancing no awe phoenix come ceremony's beauty; retreating no hawk kite strike capture's use; pacing Xiang rivers—about to become strange bird.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng wrote Huan Wen a letter in reckless vein, saying the province had sent an investigator who was neither a phoenix of good omen nor a hunting hawk—only a odd bird flapping along the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 溫得盛箋，復遣從事重案之，髒私鋃籍，檻車收盛到州，舍而不罪。

translations.literal: Wen obtained Sheng's note; again sent attendant heavily investigate; dirty private affairs in disorder; caged cart seized Sheng arrived province; released and did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen ordered a second investigation, turned up Sun Sheng's irregular profits, and had him carted to headquarters in a prison wagon—then let him go without sentence.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書監，加給事中。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to palace secretary supervisor; added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervisor of the palace library with additional appointment as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 年七十二卒。

translations.literal: Age seventy-two died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 盛篤學不倦，自少至老，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Sheng devoted learning unwearied; from youth to old age, hand did not release scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng studied tirelessly from youth to old age and never laid a book aside.

sentences.zh: 著《魏氏春秋》、《晉陽秋》，並造詩賦論難復數十篇。

translations.literal: Composed Wei Clan Spring and Autumn, Jin Yang Autumn; together made poems rhapsodies treatises disputation again several tens of chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Spring and Autumn of Wei and the Jin Yangqiu, plus several dozen poems, rhapsodies, essays, and polemics.

sentences.zh: 《晉陽秋》詞直而理正，咸稱良史焉。

translations.literal: Jin Yang Autumn phrasing straight yet principle correct; all called good historian.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yangqiu was blunt yet fair, and everyone hailed it as the work of a true historian.

sentences.zh: 既而桓溫見之，怒謂盛子曰：「枋頭誠為失利，何至乃如尊君所說！

translations.literal: Soon Huan Wen saw it; angrily said to Sheng's son, "Bangtou indeed was losing; how reach thus as your honored father said!"
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen read it he was furious and told Sun Sheng's son, "The Fangtou campaign was a setback, but how could it be as bad as your father wrote!"

sentences.zh: 若此史遂行，自是關君門戶事。

translations.literal: If this history then circulates, from this concerns your lord clan's gates and doors.
translations.idiomatic: If this history goes out, it will be your family's neck on the line."

sentences.zh: 」其子遽拜謝，謂請刪改之。

translations.literal: His son hastily bowed thanks, said beg to delete and revise it.
translations.idiomatic: The son kowtowed and begged leave to revise the text.

sentences.zh: 時盛年老還家，性方嚴有軌憲，雖子孫白，而庭訓愈峻。

translations.literal: At the time Sheng old age returned home; nature upright strict had model law; although sons grandsons white-haired, yet courtyard instruction more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng was old and home by then, stern and principled; even when his grandchildren were gray, his household discipline grew harsher.

sentences.zh: 至此，諸子乃共號泣稽顙，請為百口切計。

translations.literal: Reaching here, various sons then together wailed and knocked forehead, begged for hundred mouths urgent plan.
translations.idiomatic: At that his sons wept and knocked their heads on the ground, pleading for the whole clan's safety.

sentences.zh: 盛大怒。

translations.literal: Sheng greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng exploded with rage.

sentences.zh: 諸子遂爾改之。

translations.literal: Various sons then thus changed it.
translations.idiomatic: His sons altered the text anyway.

sentences.zh: 盛寫兩定本，寄于慕容俊。

translations.literal: Sheng wrote two fixed copies, sent to Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng made two fair copies of the original and sent them to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 太元中，孝武帝博求異聞，始於遼東得之，以相考校，多有不同，書遂兩存。

translations.literal: In Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu broadly sought strange hearsay; first from Liaodong obtained them; to mutually examine and collate; much had differences; book then two preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu cast a wide net for rare texts and recovered a copy from Liaodong. Compared with the court version, the two differed widely, so both were kept.

sentences.zh: 子潛、放。

translations.literal: Sons Qian, Fang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Sun Qian and Sun Fang.

translations.literal: Equals sign placed as a break in the transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: The manuscript marks an editorial section break with this sign alone.

sentences.zh: 子潛、放

translations.literal: Sons Qian, Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Sun Qian and Sun Fang

sentences.zh: =潛字齊由，為豫章太守。

translations.literal: Qian courtesy name Qiyou, was Yuzhang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, courtesy name Qiyou, served as Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪之討王國寶也，潛時在郡，仲堪逼以為諮議參軍，固辭不就，以憂卒。

translations.literal: When Yin Zhongkan attacked Wang Guobao, Qian was then in commandery; Zhongkan forced him as advisory army adviser; firmly declined did not take up; died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: During Yin Zhongkan's campaign against Wang Guobao, Sun Qian was in his post. Yin Zhongkan pressed him to serve as advisory army adviser; he refused steadfastly and died of distress.

sentences.zh: 放字齊莊，幼稱令慧。

translations.literal: Fang courtesy name Qizhuang; in youth called fine cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fang, courtesy name Qizhuang, was celebrated as a bright child.

sentences.zh: 年七八歲，在荊州，與父俱從庾亮獵，亮謂曰：「君亦來邪？

translations.literal: Age seven or eight, in Jing Province, with father both followed Yu Liang hunt; Liang said to him, "You lord also came?"
translations.idiomatic: At seven or eight, in Jing province, he went hunting with his father and Yu Liang. Yu Liang said, "You came along too?"

sentences.zh: 」應聲答曰：「無小無大，從公於邁。

translations.literal: Answering voice replied, "No small no large; follow lord on march."
translations.idiomatic: He answered at once, "Young or old, we follow our lord on the road."

sentences.zh: 」亮又問：「欲齊何莊邪？

translations.literal: Liang again asked, "Wish to equal which Zhuang?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked, "Whose 'Zhuang' do you wish to match?"

sentences.zh: 」放曰：「欲齊莊周。

translations.literal: Fang said, "Wish to equal Zhuang Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fang said, "Zhuang Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「不慕仲尼邪？

translations.literal: Liang said, "Not admire Zhongni?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang said, "Do you not admire Confucius?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「仲尼生而知之，非希企所及。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Zhongni born then knew it—not hope and reach what can attain."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Confucius was born knowing; no one can aspire that high."

sentences.zh: 」亮大奇之，曰：「王輔嗣弗過也。

translations.literal: Liang greatly marveled at him, said, "Wang Fusi not surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang was astonished. "Wang Bi himself would not surpass this child."

sentences.zh: 」庾翼子爰客嘗候盛，見放而問曰：「安國何在？

translations.literal: Yu Yi's son Aike once visited Sheng; saw Fang and asked, "Anguo where?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Aike, son of Yu Yi, once called on Sun Sheng, saw Sun Fang, and asked, "Where is Anguo?"

sentences.zh: 」放答曰：「庾稚恭家。

translations.literal: Fang replied, "Yu Zhigong's house."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fang answered, "At Zhigong's house."

sentences.zh: 」爰客大笑曰：「諸孫太盛，有兒如此也！

translations.literal: Aike greatly laughed saying, "Various Suns too splendid—having son like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Aike roared with laughter: "The Sun clan is thriving—to raise a boy like this!"

sentences.zh: 」放又曰：「未若諸庾翼翼。

translations.literal: Fang again said, "Not like various Yus' wing-wing."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fang added, "Still not as fine as the Yu cousins, wing beside wing."

sentences.zh: 」既而語人曰：「我故得重呼奴父也。

translations.literal: Soon told people saying, "I thus got again call slave father."
translations.idiomatic: Later he told someone, "So I got to call him 'slave's father' a second time."

sentences.zh: 」終於長沙相。

translations.literal: Ended as Changsha chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as chancellor of Changsha princedom.

sentences.zh: 干寶

translations.literal: Gan Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao

sentences.zh: 干寶，字令升，新蔡人也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao, courtesy name Lingsheng, was a man of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao, courtesy name Lingsheng, came from Xincai.

sentences.zh: 祖統，吳奮武將軍、都亭侯。

translations.literal: Grandfather Tong, Wu General Who Rouses Might, Metropolitan Village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gan Tong was Wu's General Who Rouses Might and marquis of Metropolitan Village.

sentences.zh: 父瑩，丹陽丞。

translations.literal: Father Ying, Danyang aide.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gan Ying was an aide in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 寶少勤學，博覽書記，以才器召為著作郎。

translations.literal: Bao in youth diligent in learning, broad viewed documents; by talent capacity summoned as drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao studied hard and read widely; for his ability he was summoned as a drafter.

sentences.zh: 平杜弢有功，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Pacifying Du Tao had merit; granted noble rank marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: For helping to defeat Du Tao he was enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 中興草創，未置史官，中書監王導上疏曰：「夫帝王之跡，莫不必書，著為令典，垂之無窮。

translations.literal: Restoration founding, not yet placed historians; palace secretariat supervisor Wang Dao submitted memorial saying, "Now emperor-kings' traces, none not must be written; manifest as fine canon; hang down without end."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the restoration no history office existed. Wang Dao, the palace secretariat supervisor, memorialized: "The deeds of emperors must all be recorded, set down as a lasting code for endless ages."

sentences.zh: 宣皇帝廓定四海，武皇帝受禪于魏，至德大勳，等蹤上聖，而紀傳不存於王府，德音未被乎管弦。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan broadened and settled four seas; Emperor Wu received abdication from Wei; utmost virtue great merit, equal traces upper sages—yet annals and biographies not stored in king's house; virtuous sounds not covered by strings and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan pacified the realm and Emperor Wu received the Wei abdication—virtue and achievement matching the ancient sages—yet their annals do not fill the royal archive and their praise is not sung in music."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖明，當中興之盛，宜建立國史，撰集帝紀，上敷祖宗之烈，下紀佐命之勳，務以實錄，為後代之准，厭率土之望，悅人神之心，斯誠雍熙之至美，王者之弘基也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sagely bright, facing restoration's splendor, ought establish state history, compile and gather imperial annals; above spread ancestors' fierceness; below record assist-mandate's merit; strive with true records; as later generation's standard; satisfy whole realm's hope; please human and spirit hearts—this truly is harmonious brightness's utmost beauty, king's great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules in the full flower of the restoration: found a national history, compile the reign annals, glorify the ancestors above and the founding ministers below, aim at truthful record as a model for posterity, answer the hopes of the land and gladden gods and men—that is the crown of peace and the true foundation of kingship."

sentences.zh: 宜備史官，敕佐著作郎干寶等漸就撰集。

translations.literal: Ought complete historians; order aide drafter Gan Bao and others gradually approach compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint historians and instruct assistant drafter Gan Bao and his colleagues to begin the compilation."

sentences.zh: 」元帝納焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 寶於是始領國史。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon first headed state history.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao thereupon took charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 以家貧，求補山陰令，遷始安太守。

translations.literal: Because family poor, sought supplement Shanyin magistrate; promoted Shian Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he asked for appointment as magistrate of Shanyin and later became Administrator of Shian.

sentences.zh: 王導請為司徒右長史，遷散騎常侍，著《晉紀》，自宣帝迄於湣帝五十三年，凡二十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: Wang Dao requested him as Minister of Education right chief clerk; promoted regular cavalier attendant; composed Jin Annals, from Emperor Xuan down to Emperor Min fifty-three years, in all twenty scrolls; presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao had him named chief clerk to the minister of education; he rose to regular cavalier attendant and wrote the Jin Annals in twenty scrolls from Emperor Xuan through Emperor Min—fifty-three years—which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其書簡略，直而能婉，咸稱良史。

translations.literal: His book brief and summary; straight yet able to be subtle; all called good historian.
translations.idiomatic: The work is concise, forthright yet tactful, and was praised as a master history.

sentences.zh: 性好陰陽術數，留思京房、夏侯勝等傳。

translations.literal: Nature loved yin-yang arts and numbers; lingered thought on Jing Fang, Xiahou Sheng and others' traditions.
translations.idiomatic: He loved cosmology and numerology and pondered the traditions of Jing Fang, Xiahou Sheng, and their school.

sentences.zh: 寶父先有所寵侍婢，母甚妒忌，及父亡，母乃生推婢於墓中。

translations.literal: Bao's father earlier had favored serving maid; mother very jealous; when father died, mother then alive pushed maid into tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's father had favored a concubine; his jealous mother, when the father died, had the girl sealed alive in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 寶兄弟年小，不之審也。

translations.literal: Bao brothers age small; did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao and his brothers were young and knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，母喪，開墓，而婢伏棺如生，載還，經日乃蘇。

translations.literal: After over ten years, mother's mourning; opened tomb; yet maid crouched on coffin as if alive; carried back; after a day then revived.
translations.idiomatic: More than a decade later, when his mother died and the tomb was opened, the girl was found crouched on the coffin as if alive. She was carried home and revived after a day.

sentences.zh: 言其父常取飲食與之，恩情如生，在家中吉凶輒語之，考校悉驗，地中亦不覺為惡。

translations.literal: Said her father constantly took drink and food and gave her; kindness as if alive; at home good and ill always told her; examine and collate all verified; in earth also did not feel it evil.
translations.idiomatic: She said the father had brought her food in the tomb and treated her as when he lived; back in the house she foretold fortune and misfortune and was always right, and she had not suffered underground.

sentences.zh: 既而嫁之，生子。

translations.literal: Then married her; bore son.
translations.idiomatic: She was married off and bore a child.

sentences.zh: 又寶兄嘗病氣絕，積日不冷，後遂悟，雲見天地間鬼神事，如夢覺，不自知死。

translations.literal: Also Bao's elder brother once ill breath cut off; piled days not cold; later then awakened; said saw heaven and earth between ghosts and spirits affairs; like dream awake; not self-know death.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's elder brother once lay breathless for days without growing cold, then woke and described visions of spirits between heaven and earth like a dream—unaware he had died.

sentences.zh: 寶以此遂撰集古今神祇靈異人物變化。

translations.literal: Bao by this then compiled and gathered ancient and modern spirits' numinous transformations of persons and things.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis Gan Bao collected tales of gods, marvels, and strange transformations past and present.

sentences.zh: 名為《搜神記》，凡三十卷。

translations.literal: Named In Search of the Supernatural; in all thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He titled it In Search of the Supernatural—thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 以示劉惔，惔曰：「卿可謂鬼之董狐。

translations.literal: To show Liu Tan; Tan said, "You lord can be called ghosts' Dong Hu."
translations.idiomatic: He showed it to Liu Tan, who said, "You are the Dong Hu of the spirit world."

sentences.zh: 」寶既博采異同，遂混虛實，因作序以陳其志曰：

translations.literal: Bao having broadly gathered same and different, then mixed empty and solid; therefore composed preface to state his intent saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao had gathered conflicting accounts and mingled fact with fable; he wrote a preface explaining his purpose:

sentences.zh: 寶又為《春秋左氏義外傳》，注《周易》、《周官》凡數十篇，及雜文集皆行於世。

translations.literal: Bao also composed Spring and Autumn Zuo Meaning Outer Tradition; annotated Zhou Changes, Zhou Offices in all several tens of chapters; and mixed prose collection all circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an Outer Tradition on the Meaning of the Zuo Commentary, annotated the Zhou Changes and the Offices of Zhou in several dozen chapters, and left a collection of miscellaneous essays—all of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 鄧粲

translations.literal: Deng Can.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Can

sentences.zh: 鄧粲，長沙人。

translations.literal: Deng Can, Changsha man.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Can was a native of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 少以高潔著名，與南陽劉驎之、南郡劉尚公同志友善，並不應州郡辟命。

translations.literal: In youth by high purity was famous; with Nanyang Liu Linzhi, Nanjun Liu Shanggong same aspiration friendly; together did not answer province commandery summons.
translations.idiomatic: Known young for lofty integrity, he was friends with Liu Linzhi of Nanyang and Liu Shanggong of Nanjun; none would accept provincial or commandery appointments.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓沖卑辭厚禮請粲為別駕，粲嘉其好賢，乃起應召。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector Huan Chong with humble words thick gifts requested Can as aide-de-camp; Can praised his love of worthies; then rose answering summons.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Huan Chong of Jing province wooed him with humble words and rich gifts for the post of aide-de-camp. Deng Can honored his respect for talent and accepted.

sentences.zh: 驎之、尚公謂之曰：「卿道廣學深，眾所推懷，忽然改節，誠失所望。

translations.literal: Linzhi, Shanggong said to him, "Your lord's Way broad learning deep; crowd's pushed embrace; suddenly change integrity—truly loses what was hoped."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Linzhi and Liu Shanggong told him, "Your learning is wide and admired by all; to change course so suddenly disappoints us."

sentences.zh: 」粲笑答曰：「足下可謂有志於隱而未知隱。

translations.literal: Can smiled and replied, "You sirs can be said to have aspiration toward reclusion yet not know reclusion."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Can smiled: "You wish to be recluses but do not understand reclusion."

sentences.zh: 夫隱之為道，朝亦可隱，市亦可隱。

translations.literal: Now reclusion as Way: court also can recluse; market also can recluse.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of reclusion may be practiced at court or in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 隱初在我，不在於物。

translations.literal: Reclusion at first lies in self, not in things.
translations.idiomatic: Reclusion is in the mind, not in the place."

sentences.zh: 」尚公等無以難之，然粲亦於此名譽減半矣，後患足疾，不能朝拜，求去職，不聽，令臥視事。

translations.literal: Shanggong and others had nothing to challenge him; yet Can also at this fame and reputation halved; later met foot illness; could not court bow; sought leave office; not heard; ordered lie and attend affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They could not refute him, but Deng Can's reputation was cut in half. Later, crippled by foot trouble, he could not attend court and asked to resign; permission was denied, and he was told to conduct business from bed.

sentences.zh: 後以病篤，乞骸骨，許之。

translations.literal: Later because illness critical, begged bones; permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness worsened he asked to retire and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 粲以父騫有忠信言而世無知者，著《元明紀》十篇，注《老子》，並行於世。

translations.literal: Can because father Qian had loyal trustworthy words yet age none knew; composed Yuan Ming Annals ten chapters; annotated Laozi; together circulated in age.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Deng Qian had spoken with loyalty and good faith but was forgotten, Deng Can wrote ten chapters of Yuan–Ming Annals and a commentary on the Laozi—both circulated.

sentences.zh: 謝沈

translations.literal: Xie Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chen

sentences.zh: 謝沈，字行思，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Xie Chen, courtesy name Xingsi, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chen, courtesy name Xingsi, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 曾祖斐，吳豫章太守。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Fei, Wu Yuzhang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xie Fei was Wu's Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 父秀，吳翼正都尉。

translations.literal: Father Xiu, Wu Rectifying Capital commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie Xiu was Wu's capital commandant of the rectifying wing.

sentences.zh: 沈少孤，事母至孝，博學多識，明練經史。

translations.literal: Chen young orphaned; served mother utmost filial piety; broad learning much knowledge; clear practiced classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was devoted to his mother, learned widely, and mastered the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 郡命為主簿、功曹，察孝廉，太尉郗鑒辟，並不就。

translations.literal: Commandery ordered as chief clerk, merit clerk; investigated Filial and Incorrupt; Grand Commandant Xi Jian summoned; together did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery made him chief clerk and merit assessor, nominated him Filial and Incorrupt, and Grand Commandant Xi Jian summoned him—he refused every post.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史何充引為參軍，以母老去職。

translations.literal: Kuaiji internal historian He Chong drew him as army adviser; because mother old left office.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, internal historian of Kuaiji, took him as army adviser; he resigned when his mother aged.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍庾亮命為功曹，征北將軍蔡謨版為參軍，皆不就。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Yu Liang ordered as merit clerk; General Who Conquers the North Cai Mo tablet as army adviser; all did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, the General Who Pacifies the West, named him merit clerk; Cai Mo, the General Who Conquers the North, offered him an army advisership on emergency commission—he took neither.

sentences.zh: 閒居養母，不交人事，耕耘之暇，研精墳籍。
