translations.literal: Idle dwelt nurturing mother, did not mingle human affairs; plowing and hoeing's leisure; grind fine tomb writings.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly, cared for his mother, shunned office, and between farm chores studied the classics.

sentences.zh: 康帝即位，朝議疑七廟迭毀，乃以太學博士徵，以質疑滯。

translations.literal: Emperor Kang ascended; court debate doubted seven temples' successive destruction; then by Imperial Academy erudite summoned; to resolve doubtful blockages.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Kang took the throne, court debate stalled on the rite of cycling destruction among seven ancestral temples; Xie Chen was summoned as an Imperial Academy erudite to settle the doubts.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because mother's mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除尚書度支郎。

translations.literal: Mourning ended; appointed Masters of Writing revenue gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became a revenue gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 何充、庾冰並稱沉有史才，遷著作郎，撰《晉書》三十餘卷。

translations.literal: He Chong, Yu Bing together called Chen had historian talent; promoted drafter; composed Jin Book thirty-odd chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong and Yu Bing both pronounced Xie Chen a born historian; he was promoted drafter and wrote more than thirty chapters of a Jin history.

sentences.zh: 會卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Met death; at the time age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 沉先著《後漢書》百卷及《毛詩》、《漢書外傳》，所著述及詩賦文論皆行於世。

translations.literal: Chen first composed Later Han Book hundred chapters and Mao Odes, Han Book Outer Tradition; what he wrote and poems rhapsodies essays treatises all circulated in age.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had written a hundred-chapter Later Han history, works on the Mao Odes and an outer commentary to the Han history; his essays, poems, and treatises all circulated.

sentences.zh: 其才學在虞預之右云。

translations.literal: His talent learning was at Yu Yu's right—it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship was reckoned superior to Yu Yu's.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒，字彥威，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi, courtesy name Yanwei, was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi, courtesy name Yanwei, was from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 宗族富盛，世為鄉豪。

translations.literal: Clan kin rich and flourishing; generations were village magnates.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was wealthy and for generations had been local magnates.

sentences.zh: 鑿齒少有志氣，博學洽聞，以文筆著稱。

translations.literal: Zuochi in youth had ambition and spirit; broad learning comprehensive hearing; by literary brush famed.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious from youth, widely read, he was famed for his pen.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓溫辟為從事，江夏相袁喬深器之，數稱其才于溫，轉西曹主簿，親遇隆密。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector Huan Wen summoned as retainer; Jiangxia chancellor Yuan Qiao deeply esteemed him; several times praised his talent to Wen; transferred west bureau chief clerk; intimate treatment lofty and close.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Huan Wen of Jing province took him as a retainer. Yuan Qiao, chancellor of Jiangxia, thought the world of him and praised him repeatedly to Huan Wen. Xi Zuochi became chief clerk of the western bureau and enjoyed the warmest confidence.

sentences.zh: 時溫有大志，追蜀人知天文者至，夜執手問國家祚運修短。

translations.literal: At the time Wen had great ambition; summoned Shu man who knew astronomy; night held hand asking state's fortune span long and short.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen harbored great designs. He summoned a Shu stargazer and by night took his hand, asking how long the dynasty would last.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「世祀方永。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "Generations' sacrifice just long."
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, "The house will endure for ages."

sentences.zh: 」疑其難言，乃飾辭云：「如君言，豈獨吾福，乃蒼生之幸。

translations.literal: Suspected him hard to speak; then polished words saying, "As you lord say—how only my fortune—it is the black-haired masses' luck."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen suspected he was holding back and coaxed him: "If that is so, it is not my fortune alone but the blessing of the people."

sentences.zh: 然今日之語自可令盡，必有小小厄運，亦宜說之。

translations.literal: Yet today's words from self can make exhaust; must have small small ill luck—also ought speak it.
translations.idiomatic: Speak plainly: if there is any minor ill omen, you should say so."

sentences.zh: 」星人曰：「太微、紫微、文昌三宮氣候如此，決無憂虞。

translations.literal: Star man said, "Grand Tenuity, Purple Tenuity, Culture Illumination three palaces' qi and weather thus—decidedly no worry."
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer said, "The configurations of the Grand Tenuity, Purple Palace, and Civil Office stars show no cause for fear."

sentences.zh: 至五十年外不論耳。

translations.literal: Reach fifty years beyond not discuss ear.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond fifty years I will not speak."

sentences.zh: 」溫不悅，乃止。

translations.literal: Wen not pleased; then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was displeased and dropped the subject.

sentences.zh: 異日，送絹一匹、錢五千文以與之。

translations.literal: Another day, sent silk one bolt, cash five thousand cash to give him.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he sent the man one bolt of silk and five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 星人乃馳詣鑿齒曰：「家在益州，被命遠下，今受旨自裁，無由致其骸骨。

translations.literal: Star man then galloped to Zuochi saying, "Home in Yizhou; received order far down; now received order self-cut—no means bring back bones."
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer rushed to Xi Zuochi: "My home is in Yizhou; I was ordered south. Now I am commanded to kill myself and cannot bring my bones home."

sentences.zh: 緣君仁厚，乞為標碣棺木耳。

translations.literal: Because you lord kind and thick, beg to mark stele coffin wood ear.
translations.idiomatic: You are kind—please mark my grave and supply a coffin."

sentences.zh: 」鑿齒問其故，星人曰：「賜絹一匹，令僕自裁，惠錢五千，以買棺耳。

translations.literal: Zuochi asked the reason; star man said, "Granted silk one bolt, ordered servant self-cut; grace cash five thousand, to buy coffin ear."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi asked what he meant. The man said, "One bolt of silk means I am to hang myself; five thousand cash buys the coffin."

sentences.zh: 」鑿齒曰：「君幾誤死！

translations.literal: Zuochi said, "You lord nearly wrongly died!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi cried, "You nearly killed yourself for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 君嘗聞前知星宿有不覆之義乎？

translations.literal: Have you lord once heard that foreknowing stars and constellations has a meaning of not overturning?
translations.idiomatic: Surely you have heard that a true star reader does not go back on his own reading.

sentences.zh: 此以絹戲君，以錢供道中資，是聽君去耳。

translations.literal: This with silk teases you lord; with cash supplies road travel funds—is listening to you lord depart.
translations.idiomatic: The silk was his joke; the cash is travel money. He is letting you go.

sentences.zh: 」星人大喜，明便詣溫別。

translations.literal: Star man greatly pleased; next day then visited Wen to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer was overjoyed and next day took leave of Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫問去意，以鑿齒言答。

translations.literal: Wen asked leaving intent; with Zuochi's words answered.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen asked why he was leaving; he repeated Xi Zuochi's explanation.

sentences.zh: 溫笑曰：「鑿齒憂君誤死，君定是誤活。

translations.literal: Wen smiled saying, "Zuochi worried you lord wrongly die; you lord surely are wrongly alive.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen laughed: "Xi Zuochi feared you would die by mistake—you nearly died of stupidity.

sentences.zh: 然徒三十年看儒書，不如一詣習主簿。」

translations.literal: Yet vainly thirty years reading Confucian books—not equal one visit to Xi chief clerk."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years of Confucian books are worth less than one talk with Chief Clerk Xi."

sentences.zh: 累遷別駕。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 溫出征伐，鑿齒或從或守，所在任職，每處機要，蒞事有績，善尺牘論議，溫甚器遇之。

translations.literal: When Wen campaigned, Zuochi sometimes followed sometimes guarded; wherever posted, each place critical; attending affairs had merit; good at letters and debate; Wen greatly esteemed and treated him.
translations.idiomatic: On Huan Wen's campaigns Xi Zuochi either went with the army or held the rear; every post was sensitive, and he performed well. Skilled at memorials and debate, he enjoyed Huan Wen's deepest favor.

sentences.zh: 時清談文章之士韓伯、伏滔等並相友善，後使至京師。

translations.literal: At the time pure talk literary essay gentlemen Han Bo, Fu Tao and others together mutually friendly; later envoy arrived capital.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended pure-conversation men of letters such as Han Bo and Fu Tao, and later went on mission to the capital.

sentences.zh: 簡文亦雅重焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen also elegantly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen thought highly of him as well.

sentences.zh: 既還，溫問：「相王何似？

translations.literal: After returning, Wen asked, "Minister-king how like?
translations.idiomatic: Back from the capital, Huan Wen asked, "What is the minister-king like?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「生平所未見。

translations.literal: Replied saying, "In life never seen.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have never seen his like.

sentences.zh: 」以此大忤溫旨，左遷戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: By this greatly violated Wen's intent; demoted left to revenue bureau army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: That answer deeply offended Huan Wen, who demoted him to army adviser in the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 時有桑門釋道安，俊辯有高才，自北至荊州，與鑿齒初相見。

translations.literal: At the time there was shramana Shi Daoan, handsome debate had high talent; from north arrived Jing Province; with Zuochi first met.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Shi Daoan, a brilliant debater, came from the north to Jing province and met Xi Zuochi for the first time.

sentences.zh: 道安曰：「彌天釋道安。

translations.literal: Daoan said, "Heaven-filling Shi Daoan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoan introduced himself: "I am Shi Daoan, who fills heaven.

sentences.zh: 」鑿齒曰：「四海習鑿齒。

translations.literal: Zuochi said, "Four seas Xi Zuochi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi replied: "I am Xi Zuochi, who fills the four seas.

sentences.zh: 」時人以為佳對。

translations.literal: People of the time thought it fine parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised the exchange as a perfect riposte.

sentences.zh: 初，鑿齒與其二舅羅崇、羅友俱為州從事。

translations.literal: At first, Zuochi with his two maternal uncles Luo Chong, Luo You together were province retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi and his maternal uncles Luo Chong and Luo You all served as provincial retainers.

sentences.zh: 及遷別駕，以坐越舅右，屢經陳請。

translations.literal: When promoted aide-de-camp, because seating surpassed uncles' right, repeatedly submitted requests.
translations.idiomatic: When promoted aide-de-camp he outranked his uncles in seating—a breach he repeatedly tried to excuse.

sentences.zh: 溫後激怒既盛，乃超拔其二舅，相繼為襄陽都督，出鑿齒為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: After Wen's anger flared full, then leap-promoted his two uncles; in succession became Xiangyang commanders; sent Zuochi out as Yingyang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen's rage peaked, he leapfrogged both uncles to command Xiangyang in turn and posted Xi Zuochi away as Administrator of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 溫弟秘亦有才氣，素與鑿齒相親善。

translations.literal: Wen's younger brother Mi also had talent and spirit; always with Zuochi mutually intimate and good.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's brother Huan Mi was talented and had long been close to Xi Zuochi.

sentences.zh: 鑿齒既罷郡歸，與秘書曰：

translations.literal: Zuochi having dismissed command returned; wrote to Mi a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his command Xi Zuochi wrote to Huan Mi:

sentences.zh: 其風期俊邁如此。

translations.literal: His manner and expectation lofty and grand thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the lofty tone of that letter.

sentences.zh: 是時溫覬覦非望，鑿齒在郡，著《漢晉春秋》以裁正之。

translations.literal: At the time Wen eyed beyond hope; Zuochi in commandery; composed Han Jin Spring and Autumn to judge and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was nursing imperial ambitions. Xi Zuochi, still in his command, wrote the Han–Jin Spring and Autumn to set the moral record straight.

sentences.zh: 起漢光武，終於晉湣帝。

translations.literal: Rose from Han Guangwu; ended at Jin Min Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: It ran from Han Guangwu to Emperor Min of Jin.

sentences.zh: 于三國之時，蜀以宗室為正，魏武雖受漢禪晉，尚為篡逆，至文帝平蜀，乃為漢亡而晉始興焉。

translations.literal: In Three Kingdoms time, Shu by imperial house was orthodox; Wei martial although received Han abdication Jin, still was usurpation; reaching Wendi pacifying Shu—then was Han perished and Jin began to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Three Kingdoms he treated Shu, as heir to the Han house, as holding the true mandate. Wei had taken the Han abdication and Jin had succeeded Wei, yet both remained usurpation until Jin Wendi conquered Shu—only then did Han truly end and Jin's rise stand justified.

sentences.zh: 引世祖諱炎興而為禪受，明天心不可以勢力強也。

translations.literal: Cited heir-apparent's taboo Yanxing as abdication acceptance; clarifying heaven's heart cannot by force and power be compelled.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Shu ruler's reign motto Yanxing and the peaceful handover to show that Heaven's intent cannot be forced by mere power.

sentences.zh: 凡五十四卷。

translations.literal: In all fifty-four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-four scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 後以腳疾，遂廢於里巷。

translations.literal: Later because foot illness; then cast aside in lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Crippled by foot trouble, he lived out his days in retirement.

sentences.zh: 及襄陽陷於苻堅，堅素聞其名，與道安俱輿而致焉。

translations.literal: When Xiangyang fell to Fu Jian; Jian always heard his name; with Daoan together in sedan brought him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang fell to Fu Jian, the king, who had long admired him, had him brought in a litter alongside Daoan.

sentences.zh: 既見，與語，大悅之，賜遺甚厚。

translations.literal: After meeting, spoke with him; greatly pleased; gifts very generous.
translations.idiomatic: They talked; Fu Jian was delighted and showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 又以其蹇疾，與諸鎮書：「昔晉氏平吳，利在二陸；

translations.literal: Also because his lame illness; to various garrisons wrote letter: "Formerly Jin clan pacified Wu; profit lay in two Lus;
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi Zuochi was lame, Fu Jian wrote the garrisons: "When Jin conquered Wu, the prize was the two Lus;

sentences.zh: 今破漢南，獲士裁一人有半耳。

translations.literal: now breaking south of Han; obtained scholars only one person plus half ear.
translations.idiomatic: now that south of the Han is taken, I have gained one and a half worthy men."

sentences.zh: 」俄以疾歸襄陽。

translations.literal: Soon because illness returned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to Xiangyang on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋而襄鄧反正，朝廷欲徵鑿齒，使典國史，會卒，不果。

translations.literal: Soon Xiangyang and Deng returned to allegiance; court wished to summon Zuochi, make him oversee state history; met death; not realized.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang and Deng returned to Jin, the court meant to recall him to head the national history, but he died before it happened.

sentences.zh: 臨終上疏曰：

translations.literal: On verge of death submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣每謂皇晉宜越魏繼漢，不應以魏後為三恪。

translations.literal: Your subject always said imperial Jin ought leap Wei and succeed Han; ought not take Wei heirs as three reverent houses.
translations.idiomatic: I have always held that legitimate Jin should bypass Wei to continue Han, and that Wei should not be honored among the three reverent former dynasties.

sentences.zh: 而身微官卑，無由上達，懷抱愚情，三十餘年。

translations.literal: Yet body slight office low; no means ascend and reach; bosom holds foolish feeling—thirty odd years.
translations.idiomatic: Low in rank, I could not get a hearing; this conviction has burned in me for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 今沈淪重疾，性命難保，遂嘗懷此，當與之朽爛，區區之情，切所悼惜，謹力疾著論一篇，寫上如左。

translations.literal: Now sunk in grave illness; life hard to protect; then ever held this—about to with it rot away; petty feeling—keenly what I mourn; respectfully with effort despite illness composed treatise one piece; write present as left.
translations.idiomatic: Now I sink under mortal illness and may die with this unspoken—grief to me. Though sick I have drafted the essay below.

sentences.zh: 願陛下考尋古義，求經常之表，超然遠覽，不以臣微賤廢其所言。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty examine seek ancient meaning; seek constant norm's surface; transcendently far view; not because subject mean and low discard what is said.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to search the classical precedents for the enduring standard, to see far beyond my low station, and not dismiss my words.

sentences.zh: 論曰：

translations.literal: Treatise said:
translations.idiomatic: The essay begins:

sentences.zh: 子辟強，才學有父風，位至驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: Son Pijiang; talent learning had father's manner; position reached cavalry-in-attendant retainer gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi Pijiang inherited his gifts and rose to retainer gentleman to the cavalry-in-attendant.

sentences.zh: 徐廣

translations.literal: Xu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang

sentences.zh: 徐廣，字野民，東莞姑幕人，侍中邈之弟也。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, courtesy name Yemin, was a man of Gumu in Dongguan; Palace Attendant Miao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang, courtesy name Yemin, came from Gumu in Dongguan and was the younger brother of Palace Attendant Xu Miao.

sentences.zh: 世好學，至廣尤為精純，百家數術無不研覽。

translations.literal: Generations loved learning; reaching Guang especially refined and pure; hundred schools arts and numbers none not studied and viewed.
translations.idiomatic: His family were scholars; Guang was the most thorough, mastering every school and technical art.

sentences.zh: 謝玄為兗州，辟從事。

translations.literal: When Xie Xuan was Yan Province, summoned as retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan, as Inspector of Yan province, took him as a retainer.

sentences.zh: 譙王恬為鎮北，補參軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao Tian was Defender of the North; supplemented as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tian of Qiao, the Defender of the North, appointed him army adviser.

sentences.zh: 孝武世，除秘書郎，典校秘書省。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu era; appointed palace secretary gentleman; supervised collation in palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he became a gentleman of the palace library and collated texts there.

sentences.zh: 增置省職，轉員外散騎侍郎，仍領校書。

translations.literal: Added province posts; transferred supernumerary cavalier attendant; still headed collation.
translations.idiomatic: When the office expanded he became supernumerary cavalier attendant and kept charge of collation.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王珣深相欽重，舉為祠部郎，會稽世子元顯時錄尚書，欲使百僚致敬，內外順之，使廣為議，廣常以為愧焉。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing director Wang Xun deeply mutually esteemed; raised as sacrifices section gentleman; Kuaiji heir Yuanxian then recorded Masters of Writing; wished make hundred officials pay respect; inner and outer obeyed; ordered Guang draft discussion; Guang always took it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Xun of the Masters of Writing prized him and named him to the sacrifices section. When Yuanxian, heir of Kuaiji, headed the Masters of Writing and ordered the bureaucracy to bow to him, the court complied and told Xu Guang to draft the protocol—Xu Guang was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 元顯引為中軍參軍，遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: Yuanxian drew as central army army adviser; promoted garrison chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian took him as army adviser to the central army; he became chief clerk to the garrison general.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，以為大將軍文學祭酒，義熙初，奉詔撰車服儀注，除鎮軍諮議，領記室，封樂成侯，轉員外散騎常侍，領著作。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan assisted government; made him grand general literary libation; Yixi beginning; received edict compose carriage and dress ritual notes; appointed advisory to army garrison; headed secretary; enfeoffed marquis of Lecheng; transferred supernumerary regular cavalier attendant; headed drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Xuan's regency he was literary libation to the grand general. Early in Yixi he was ordered to compile regulations for carriages and dress, became adviser to the garrison general with secretary duties, was enfeoffed marquis of Lecheng, then supernumerary regular cavalier attendant in charge of drafting.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏：「左史述言，右官書事，《乘》《志》顯于晉鄭，《春秋》著乎魯史。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing memorialized: "Left historian narrates words; right official writes affairs; Sheng and Zhi shone in Jin and Zheng; Spring and Autumn appeared in Lu history.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing memorialized: "The left recorder sets down speeches, the right records events—the Sheng and Zhi made Jin and Zheng famous, and the Spring and Autumn was fixed in Lu's annals.

sentences.zh: 自聖代有造《中興記》者，道風帝典，煥乎史策。

translations.literal: Since sage age there was who made Restoration Record; way wind imperial canons; splendid in historical slips.
translations.idiomatic: Since this blessed age began, the Restoration Record has given imperial virtue radiant form in the histories.

sentences.zh: 而太和以降，世曆三朝，玄風聖跡，倏為疇古。

translations.literal: Yet from Taihe down, generations passed three courts; dark wind sage traces; suddenly became ancient past.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed; those lofty deeds are already distant memory.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳，宜敕著作郎徐廣撰成國史。

translations.literal: We ministers examined in detail; ought order drafter Xu Guang complete state history.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ask that drafter Xu Guang be charged to finish the national history.

sentences.zh: 」於是敕廣撰集焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered Guang compile and gather.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Xu Guang to compile it.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，領徐州大中正，轉正員常侍、大司家、仍領著作如故。

translations.literal: Promoted fierce cavalry general; concurrent Xu Province grand state appraiser; transferred full regular attendant, grand minister of household, still headed drafting as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted general of fierce cavalry and grand state appraiser for Xu province, then full regular attendant and grand minister of agriculture while keeping his drafting post.

sentences.zh: 十二年，勒成《晉紀》，凡四十六卷，表上之。

translations.literal: Twelfth year; completed Jin Annals; in all forty-six scrolls; memorial presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he finished the Jin Annals in forty-six scrolls and presented them.

sentences.zh: 因乞解史任，不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon begged release history duty; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved of the history office; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Promoted palace secretary supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervisor of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄篡位，帝出宮，廣陪列，悲動左右。

translations.literal: At first, Huan Xuan usurped throne; emperor left palace; Guang in attendant ranks; grief moved left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne and the emperor left the palace, Xu Guang stood in the cortège and wept so that all around were moved.

sentences.zh: 及劉裕受禪，恭帝遜位，廣獨哀感，涕泗交流。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu received abdication; Emperor Gong yielded throne; Guang alone grieved; tears and mucus crossed flow.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu took the abdication and Emperor Gong stepped down, Xu Guang alone sobbed aloud.

sentences.zh: 謝晦見之，謂曰：「徐公將無小過也。

translations.literal: Xie Hui saw him; said to him, "Lord Xu perhaps has small excess?
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui said, "Sir, are you not overdoing it a little?

sentences.zh: 」廣收淚而言曰：「君為宋朝佐命，吾乃晉室遺老，憂喜之事固不同時。

translations.literal: Guang gathered tears and spoke saying, "You lord are Song dynasty assist-mandate; I am Jin house surviving elder; sorrow and joy affairs solidly not same time.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang dried his tears: "You serve the new Song; I am an old man of Jin—our reasons to weep or smile are not the same.

sentences.zh: 」乃更歔欷。

translations.literal: Then again sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: He wept again.

sentences.zh: 因辭衰老，乞歸桑梓。

translations.literal: Thereupon declined old age; begged return mulberry and catalpa.
translations.idiomatic: Citing age, he asked to retire to his home country.

sentences.zh: 性好讀書，老猶不倦。

translations.literal: Nature loved reading; old still unwearied.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books to the end of his life.

sentences.zh: 年七十四，卒於家。

translations.literal: Age seventy-four; died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 廣《答禮問》行於世。

translations.literal: Guang's Answers to Ritual Questions circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His Answers to Questions on Ritual circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: 【Historical Essay】
translations.idiomatic: Historical essay

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古之王者咸建史臣，昭法立訓，莫近於此。

translations.literal: Historian-ministers said: Ancient king-lords all established historian-ministers; clarify law establish teaching—none nearer than this.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Every ancient king appointed official historians to clarify law and teach posterity—nothing comes closer to that duty.

sentences.zh: 若夫原始要終，紀情括性，其言微而顯，其義皎而明，然後可以茵藹緹油，作程遐世者也。

translations.literal: As for tracing origin grasping end, recording emotion summarizing nature; their words subtle yet manifest; their meanings bright yet clear—then can spread shade and crimson gloss; make model far generation.
translations.idiomatic: To trace beginnings and ends, capture motive and character, to speak subtly yet clearly and make meaning shine—then a work may ride the carriage of fame and set a distant model for the world.

sentences.zh: 丘明即沒，班馬迭興，奮鴻筆於西京，騁直詞於東觀。

translations.literal: Qiu Ming then gone; Ban and Ma in turn rose; wielded great brush in western capital; galloped straight words in Eastern View.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuo Qiuiming came Ban and Sima, wielding mighty pens in the western capital and plain words in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 自斯已降，分明競爽，可以繼明先典者，陳壽得之乎！

translations.literal: From this down; clear and bright competing splendid—can continue illuminate former canons—Chen Shou obtained it!
translations.idiomatic: Among later writers who could carry forward the great models, Chen Shou succeeded!

sentences.zh: 江漢英靈，信有之矣。

translations.literal: Yangzi and Han heroic spirits—truly there are such.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi and Han country truly breeds such genius.

sentences.zh: 允源將率之子，篤志典墳；

translations.literal: Yuanyuan general-leader's son; devoted mind to canons and tombs;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu, son of a commander, devoted himself to the classics;

sentences.zh: 紹統戚籓之胤，研機載籍。

translations.literal: Shaotong kin fence's descendant; ground subtleties in written records.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao, a kinsman of the blood princes, plumbed subtle learning in texts.

sentences.zh: 咸能綜緝文，垂諸不朽，豈必克傳門業，方擅箕裘者哉！

translations.literal: All able to weave and gather literature; hang down imperishable—must they exhaustively transmit gate enterprise, then alone excel sack and robe?
translations.idiomatic: Each wove lasting prose without needing to inherit a family office to master the craft.

sentences.zh: 處叔區區，勵精著述，混淆蕪舛，良不足觀。

translations.literal: Shushu petty; strove essence in writing; mixed confused weedy wrong—truly not worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin toiled at history, but his text is tangled and flawed—little to admire.

sentences.zh: 叔甯寡聞，穿窬王氏，雖勒成一家，未足多尚。

translations.literal: Shuning narrow hearing; bored through Wang clan; although forced complete one school—not enough much to esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu stole from Wang Yin's materials; though he finished a book, it hardly deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 令升、安國有良史之才，而所著之書惜非正典。

translations.literal: Lingsheng, Anguo had good historian's talent; yet what they composed books—alas not orthodox canons.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao and Sun Sheng had historian's gifts, yet their chief works stray from standard history.

sentences.zh: 悠悠晉室，斯文將墜。

translations.literal: Long long Jin house; this culture about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Long did the house of Jin drift; its literary culture nearly fell away.

sentences.zh: 鄧粲、謝沈祖述前史，葺宇重軒之下，施床連榻之上，奇詞異義，罕見稱焉。

translations.literal: Deng Can, Xie Chen traced and narrated former histories; thatched eaves under double eaves; spread bed on linked couch; strange phrases odd meanings—rarely seen praised.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Can and Xie Chen followed earlier models, writing under their eaves and couches—odd diction that won little praise.

sentences.zh: 習氏、徐公俱云筆削，彰善癉惡，以為懲勸。

translations.literal: Xi clan, Lord Xu both called brush trim; show good reprove evil; to serve warn and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi and Xu Guang wielded the historian's brush to praise good and blast evil for warning and example.

sentences.zh: 夫蹈忠履正，貞士之心；

translations.literal: Now tread loyalty walk straight—steadfast knight's heart;
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and rectitude are the steadfast man's way;

sentences.zh: 背義圖榮，君子不敢。

translations.literal: Betray righteousness seek glory—gentleman dares not.
translations.idiomatic: to sell principle for favor the gentleman shuns.

sentences.zh: 而彥威跡淪寇壤，逡巡于偽國；

translations.literal: Yet Yanwei's traces sank in bandit soil; hesitated in false state;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yanwei lingered in a usurper's court;

sentences.zh: 野民運遭革命，流漣於舊朝。

translations.literal: Yemin fortune met revolution; drifted attached to old court.
translations.idiomatic: Yemin clung to the fallen dynasty when heaven changed rulers.

sentences.zh: 行不違言，廣得之矣。

translations.literal: Conduct not violate speech—Guang obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang's deeds matched his words—there he succeeded.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：陳壽含章，岩岩孤峙。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Chen Shou holds pattern; lofty lone peak.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment runs: Chen Shou holds his pattern aloft like a lone peak.

sentences.zh: 彪溥勵節，摛辭綜理。

translations.literal: Biao Pu urged integrity; spread phrases weave principle.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao and Yu Pu strove for integrity and ordered their prose.

sentences.zh: 王恧雅才，虞慚惇史。

translations.literal: Wang ashamed of elegant talent; Yu shamed by honest history.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin wasted fine gifts; Yu Yu falls short of a true historian.

sentences.zh: 幹孫撫翰，前良可擬。

translations.literal: Gan Sun caress brush; former good can be compared.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao and Sun Sheng take up the brush in the track of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 鄧謝懷鉛，異聞無紀。

translations.literal: Deng Xie bosom lead; strange hearsay without record.
translations.idiomatic: Deng and Xie carried their styluses but left marvels unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 習亦研思，徐非絢美，咸被簡冊，共傳遙祀。

translations.literal: Xi also ground thought; Xu not splendid beauty; all covered by bamboo slips; together transmit distant sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi thought deeply; Xu Guang wrote plainly—yet all entered the chronicles and will be read in ages to come.
